THURSDAY - JANUARY 28, 2016 - CITY HALL -
7:00 P.M.
COUNCIL CHAMBERS, BLOOMFIELD AVENUE AT 183RD STREET
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
JANUARY 28, 2016, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Councilmember Jim Edwards.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Recreation Services Division youth basketball
  Rookie III Bandits.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair George Ray
  Mayor/Chair Carol Chen

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  Proclamations were presented as follows:

  Michael Oropeza, Senior Representative, Office of the Assessor – Executive Office
  (Homeowners’ Exemption Awareness Month – January 2016).

  Gahr High School Marching Gladiators Band (First Place and Grand Champion Division 5
  Finals of the 2015 California State Band Championships).

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Robert Suhajda commented on the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated January 28, 2016
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Pulido, to approve the Register of
  Demands for the City of Cerritos dated January 28, 2016 in the total amount of
  $9,977,686.40 (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  January 28, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 6

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands for the Successor Agency dated
  January 28, 2016 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Pulido, to approve the Register of
  Demands for the Successor Agency dated January 28, 2016 in the total amount of
  $4,032,827.24 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  January 14, 2016 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Pulido, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of January 14, 2016
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Waive full reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2016-01, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS ADOPTING A YOUTH EMPLOYMENT PLAN FOR THE
  PROPOSED LIBERTY PARK ANNEX EXTERIOR IMPROVEMENTS (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Pulido, to adopt Resolution No.
  2016-01, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
  ADOPTING A YOUTH EMPLOYMENT PLAN FOR THE PROPOSED LIBERTY PARK
  ANNEX EXTERIOR IMPROVEMENTS (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as
  follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and introduce AN ORDINANCE OF
  THE CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING CHAPTER 9.100 AND SECTION 22.40.300 OF
  THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO THE CULTIVATION AND DELIVERY
  OF MARIJUANA AND MEDICAL MARIJUANA, HEREIN REFERENCED AS
  DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2016-1 (COUNCIL)*.

  *Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA), this project is categorically exempt from CEQA review.

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager. A
  PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.
 City of Cerritos  January 28, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 6

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments. Noting there were no
  individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments and the public
  hearing.

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Pulido, to:
  1. Approve Development Code Amendment 2016-1, making the findings set forth in
  Cerritos Planning Commission Resolution No. 2016-2, and
  2. Waive reading of and introduce Ordinance No. 1002, AN ORDINANCE OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING CHAPTER 9.100 AND SECTION 22.40.300
  OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO THE CULTIVATION
  AND DELIVERY OF MARIJUANA AND MEDICAL MARIJUANA, HEREIN
  REFERENCED AS DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2016-1 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and status update of Well C-2 repair (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vince Brar, Senior Assistant City Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Approve the expenditure of funds in the amount of $423,434 for the rehabilitation
  and repair of Well C-2 to General Pump Company, and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to approve up to 5% in additional contingency funding
  necessary to complete the work. The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of award of a contract for maintenance of Cerritos
  arterial, center median and additional public landscaped areas, Bid No. 1231-16
  (COUNCIL)*.

  *Continued from the January 14, 2016 City Council Meeting.

  A staff report was given by Todd Kuh, Parks Superintendent.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.
 City of Cerritos  January 28, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 6

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Award a $374,440 contract to Complete Landscape Care, Inc. for landscape and
  irrigation maintenance of the center medians and arterial planters, and
  2. Award a $320,800 contract to Landcare for landscape and irrigation maintenance of
  Assessment District-6, Area IV-ADP-2 and freeway landscape, and
  3. Award a $53,114 contract to Valley Crest Landscape Maintenance, Inc. for
  landscape and irrigation maintenance of the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts,
  the Cerritos Senior Center and Pat Nixon Park, and City-owned property, and
  4. Reject all other bids, and
  5. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related change
  orders. (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration of award of a contract for Cerritos parkway tree
  maintenance, Bid No. 1233-16 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Todd Kuh, Parks Superintendent.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Pulido, to:
  1. Award a multi-year contract in the amount of $1,162,400 for Cerritos Parkway Tree
  Maintenance, Bid No. 1233-16, to Golden West Arbor Services, Inc., and
  2. Reject all other bids, and
  3. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related change
  orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9D.  Review and consideration of award of a contract for floor resurfacing at the Cerritos
  Center for the Performing Arts, Project No. 12719, Bid No. 1230-16 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.
 City of Cerritos  January 28, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 6

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9D.  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Pulido, to:
  1. Authorize the use of available funds originally allocated for the design of the
  South Street Sewer Rehabilitation Project for Project No. 12719: Cerritos Center
  for the Performing Arts Stage Floor Resurfacing, and
  2. Award a contract in the amount of $184,700 for Bid Item No. 1 of Cerritos Center
  for the Performing Arts Stage Floor Resurfacing, Project No. 12719, Bid No.
  1230-16, to Petra CPS, and
  3. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project related change

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen

  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9E.  Review and consideration of changing alliances from the Southeast Los Angeles
  County Workforce Development Board to the Pacific Gateway Workforce
  Development Board (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Daryl Evans, Public Safety Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Ray, to continue the City’s
  association with the Southeast Los Angeles County Workforce Development
  Board (SELACO WDB) (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10A.  Report on pending legislation

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State

  None.

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Edwards, Pulido, and Solanki, Mayor
